verdict.rationale: Context.dev has a dedicated rate-limits doc page. It confirms per-minute limits apply to authenticated API keys and that responses expose rate-limit headers, so a data engineer can find the enforced limit at runtime. The evidence pack does not state the actual numeric requests-per-minute or per-second values, or how they vary by plan or key, so the specific documented threshold remains unproven. Missing for 10: explicit numeric rate-limit values per key or plan, throttling behavior details (e.g., 429 handling or retry guidance), and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a data-engineer, I know the documented rate limit (requests per second or minute) enforced on my API key before throttling kicks in

citations.quote: Authenticated API responses expose these headers when a per-minute limit applies
